extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, attorneys, in-house counsel and patent prosecutors handling Australian filings and portfolios
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for analyzing and prosecuting inventive-step (obviousness) issues in Australian patent applications and patents, including the tripartite historic standards, tests from case law, prior-art selection rules, and prosecution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: General inventive step definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention will be taken to involve an inventive step in Australia unless it would have been obvious to a person skilled in the relevant art (PSA) in light of the common general knowledge (CGK) and the relevant prior art base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of assessment is looking forward from the prior art base to see what a PSA is likely to have done when faced with a similar problem; avoid ex post facto/hindsight analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step Standard 1 (filed 30 April 1991 – before 1 April 2002)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment based on CGK in the patent area only (i.e., Australia), optionally combined with a single piece of prior art information (a single document or act made public anywhere before the priority date) that the PSA could reasonably be expected to have "ascertained, understood and regarded ... as relevant to work in the relevant art in the patent area."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No combining/mosaicking of documents is permitted unless the PSA treats them as a 'single source of information.' Applies to some pharmaceutical patents via PTE; sunset 1 April 2027 (after which it will no longer apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step Standard 2 (filed on/after 1 April 2002; examination requested before 15 April 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment based on the CGK in Australia, optionally combined with one or more pieces of prior art information (documents or acts made public anywhere before priority date). Prior art must be reasonably expected to have been 'ascertained, understood and regarded as relevant' by the PSA (no longer limited to Australia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where combinations are relied upon, the PSA must also be reasonably expected to have combined the documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step Standard 3 (examination requested on/after 15 April 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment based on the worldwide CGK, optionally combined with one or more pieces of prior art information (worldwide). It is not required that prior art have been reasonably expected to have been 'ascertained, understood and regarded as relevant' by the PSA, but for document combinations the PSA must be reasonably expected to have combined them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader prior-art and CGK scope than Standards 1 and 2; combinations still require a reasonable expectation that PSA would combine documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for inventive step (case-law formulations and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial tests include: Wellcome/Aickin J — whether the hypothetical addressee would have taken as a matter of routine whatever steps might have led from the prior art to the invention; Aktiebolaget Hässle — steps 'as a matter of routine' exclude complex, laborious, trial-and-error courses and require that the notional research group would be directly led as a matter of course to try the claimed invention with an expectation of a useful result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not enough that an invention be 'obvious to try' — there must be a reasonable expectation of success. Recent authority (Sandoz v Bayer) emphasises that routine clinical trials can point to obviousness absent evidence of a special problem overcome. For combination claims, Minnesota Mining requires that the selection of integers (from many possibilities) itself be shown to be obvious. Apply these tests without hindsight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting point for assessing inventive step (use of specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in the specification (including the problem statement) does not enlarge the body of knowledge used to assess inventive step unless that information can be attributed to the PSA (i.e., forms part of the CGK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a patent is directed to solving a problem, that problem must be discernible from the CGK and/or prior art for it to be used as the starting point for inventive-step analysis; courts rejected enlarging the starting point by reference to the inventor's specification unless attributable to PSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of prior art documents under Standard 1 (single prior art document rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Standard 1 a single prior art document must be the piece of information added to the CGK; multiple documents can be used only to identify that one piece, but each identified document must be considered separately with the CGK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invention may be rendered obvious by combining one document with the CGK even if other documents, when combined with the CGK, would teach away. Multiple documents cannot be 'mosaicked' except to the extent they result in a single source of information the PSA would use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single source of information (when multiple documents treated as one)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more documents (or acts) may be treated as a single source of information where they can be considered 'one consistent whole' — e.g., one incorporated into another by cross-reference as shorthand for incorporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether documents form a single source depends on the nature of the art and the degree of connection between the documents; limited case law (Nicaro) — examine factual connection and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertainment, understanding and relevance (Standards 1 & 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a document or act to count under Standards 1 and 2 it must be reasonably expected to have been 'ascertained' (discovered by routine searches), 'understood' (comprehended by the PSA) and 'regarded as relevant to work in the relevant art' (the PSA would see it as relevant to solving the problem or meeting a need).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Standard 1 the requirement is qualified further: the document must be reasonably expected to have been so regarded 'to work in the relevant art in the patent area' (i.e., in Australia). On reasonable ascertainment, Sandoz clarifies that evidence need only show that the adduced searches are a subset of searches the PSA would have taken, not that the PSA preferred that information over all others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinations of documents (Standards 2 & 3) — factors for reasonable combination
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing whether a PSA would reasonably be expected to combine documents, consider factors such as whether the nature and content of the documents make combination likely, whether the documents come from similar/different/remote technical fields, and whether the art taught away from the particular combination at the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance appears in the Australian Patent Office Manual of Practice and Procedure; limited case law — apply these factors holistically when arguing for/against combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solution approach (practical prosecution steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Australian Patent Office favours a problem-solution approach that involves: (i) construing the specification to determine the problem the invention solves; (ii) identifying the relevant PSA; (iii) determining whether, in the context of the problem, any pieces of prior art could reasonably be expected to have been combined by the PSA; (iv) determining the CGK; and (v) determining whether, in the context of the problem, the claimed invention would have been obvious to the PSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step (v) typically involves applying one or more of the judicial tests for inventive step; other factors (secondary indicia) may also be considered for/against obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary indicia / factors against obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors such as practical difficulties, long-felt need, unexpected synergies, or other evidence of non-routine development may weigh against a finding of obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors are not determinative but evidence of them can assist in establishing that an invention would not be obvious to the PSA; systematically document and present such evidence during drafting and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative step standard (innovation patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation patents require only an 'innovative step' — i.e., that the claims make a substantial contribution over the prior art — a lower threshold than inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation patents: max term 8 years, up to five claims, quick grant but substantive examination and certification required for enforcement; phasing out began 26 Aug 2021 (divisional innovation patents allowed from standard applications with effective filing date before that); innovative step is easier to meet and hence often harder to invalidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline audits (practitioner action point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map pending/appealed cases against the 1 April 2027 sunset clause for Standard 1 and consider timing effects on applicable inventive-step standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether divisional claims subject to a higher inventive step standard can be incorporated into a parent patent subject to a lower standard (e.g., by narrowing post‑grant amendments); consider filing divisional innovation patent applications where permitted to strengthen position.

rubrics_metrics.name: CGK boundaries (practitioner action point)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Standard 1/2 cases, commission Australian-specific CGK analyses; for Standard 3 cases, conduct global CGK mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine geographic and technical scope of what counts as CGK for the relevant standard and document expert evidence accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination defense (practitioner action point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document technical disincentives against prior-art combinations and assess whether mosaicking or treating multiple documents as a single source is permitted under the relevant standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before prosecution/defence, record why a PSA would not combine the cited documents (different fields, taught-away teachings, lack of motivation) and, where applicable, consider arguments that documents cannot be treated as a single source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solution alignment in drafting (practitioner action point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft specifications to mirror CGK-recognised problems, avoiding or supplementing self-created technical narratives that cannot be attributed to the PSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experimental data tables to demonstrate non-routine research pathways and align the specification's problem/solution framing with what can be attributed to CGK/prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary indicia leverage (practitioner action point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically document any practical difficulties, long‑felt need, unexpected synergies or other secondary indicia during development, drafting, and prosecution to assist in rebutting obviousness attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also gather evidence to meet reasonable 'ascertainment' and 'relevance' requirements where Standards 1/2 apply; use these materials to strengthen positions in prosecution and litigation.
